entries.what_happened: Main claim, in 'Mass and covering exponents for fixed-length honeycomb walks'. Let W_n be the n-edge self-avoiding walks on the honeycomb lattice from a fixed vertex o, with uniform law P_n and free endpoint. For every δ>0 and k>0 there are C_{δ,k} and n_0(δ,k) such that for all n ≥ n_0, outside an event of P_n-probability at most C_{δ,k} n^{-k}: (i) the diameter D satisfies n^{3/4-δ} ≤ D ≤ n^{3/4+δ}; (ii) for every visited vertex z and every real s in [1,n], the number of visited vertices in the closed ball of radius s about z lies between n^{-δ} min{n, s^{4/3}} and n^{δ} min{n, s^{4/3}}; (iii) the least number N(s) of radius-s balls covering the visited set lies between n^{-δ}(1+n s^{-4/3}) and n^{δ}(1+n s^{-4/3}). Corollaries: the projection onto each lattice-normal direction has span at least n^{3/4-δ}; log N(s)/log(D/s) tends to 4/3 in probability for s up to n^{3/4-ε}; the radius of gyration R_g and the p-th moments of D and R_g are n^{3p/4+o(1)}. The proof works with the critical activity ρ=(2+√2)^{-1/2} (Duminil-Copin and Smirnov), uses the normalization c_n ρ^n ≥ 1, and passes from full-box estimates to fixed length by absolute exceptional masses; its analytic inputs come from three companion manuscripts (see conditional_on). Related manuscripts in the family: 'Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks' claims that uniform strict bridges with n visited vertices (even n) have terminal distance and diameter n^{3/4+o(1)} in probability, and that for uniform full-plane n-step walks from a fixed center, endpoint distance and maximum radius are n^{3/4+o(1)} in probability along a set of lengths of natural density one, with moments n^{3p/4+o(1)}; its every-length diameter upper bound is taken from the Mass paper. 'Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks' claims polygon diameter tails r^{-2+o(1)} (unrooted) and r^{-2/3+o(1)} (length-weighted), a truncated second length moment r^{2/3+o(1)}, and that polygons conditioned on length at least n have diameter n^{3/4+o(1)} in probability. 'Critical strip-crossing mass on the honeycomb lattice' claims total strip-crossing weight ≍ N^{-1/4} and a first displacement moment ≍ N^{3/4}. 'Uniform marked-polygon estimates and sharp finite bridge moments' claims bridge mass ≍ h^{-1/4}, first-length mass at most C h^{13/12}, and mass at least c h^{-1/4} on bridges of length at least c h^{4/3}. 'Cylinder loop weights and planar nesting' claims the cylinder partition exponent at every fixed positive loop fugacity, with exponent 1/6 at fugacity two, and planar and middle-strip nesting exponents 1/12. 'Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds' claims that the length-square mass of simple polygons of diameter at most H, modulo translations, is at most H^{2/3+o(1)}, plus a two-mark cylinder estimate and a one-arc bound. 'Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice' claims the same 1/6 and 1/12 exponents, hexagon chord partition R^{3/4+o(1)} and normalized mean length R^{4/3+o(1)}, and the same H^{2/3+o(1)} length-square bound. 'Disk transfer representations and confined bridge mass' claims strip bridge mean length R^{4/3+o(1)} (also after confinement to a multiple of the strip width), bridge mass ≍ R^{-1/4}, and half-plane arch kernel ≍ m^{-5/4}. 'Polynomial vacuum representations and bridge mass for honeycomb walks' claims strip bridge mean length h^{4/3+o(1)} under the all-length critical measure, and central visit probability R^{-2/3+o(1)} with mean length R^{4/3+o(1)} for free-boundary hexagon chords. 'Cylinder amplitudes and logarithmic bridge-length windows on the honeycomb lattice' claims that bridges with lengths between h^{4/3}(log h)^{-1/8} and 2h^{4/3}(log h)^{1/2} have mass at least h^{3/4}(log h)^{-C}, summed through height 2h(log h)^{1/64}. 'Critical honeycomb chords with prescribed boundary endpoints' claims that critical walks between prescribed ports of a regular hexagon of scale R have length R^{4/3+o(1)} in probability, with a half-plane mean of the same order. 'Cap-selected amplitudes and triangle chords for honeycomb walks' claims triangle-chord partition sum ≍ R^{3/4} with mean length R^{4/3+o(1)}, and a cylinder amplitude N^{1/6+o(1)}. The Strip, Cylinder loop weights, Marked polygon and Uniform marked-polygon claims are checked against the statements the Mass and Renewal papers quote from them; the remaining manuscripts are summarized from their abstracts only.
entries.delivers: Taken as correct, the Mass paper gives, for the uniform law on n-edge honeycomb walks from a fixed vertex, two-sided exponent-level bounds on three spatial statistics (diameter n^{3/4}, local mass s^{4/3} capped at n, covering number n s^{-4/3}), valid at every sufficiently large n with polynomially small failure probability and n^{±δ} slack for each δ>0. This describes how large a fixed-length walk is and how it fills space as a function of n, but only up to exponent-level factors: it gives no formula, no explicit constant, and no approximation with a stated error for any of the three quantities. Its scope is the honeycomb lattice only, and the exponents 3/4 and 4/3 are the predicted values, here established up to n^{±δ}. The paper does not say it settles the Wikipedia question, which asks for a function modelling the walks; its nearest claim is the 3/4 size exponent, a scaling law for the trace rather than a count, generating function or algorithm. The Renewal paper gives the corresponding endpoint and maximum-radius law for uniform full-plane n-step walks only along a set of lengths of natural density one; its strict-bridge result (even n) is for a different ensemble. The Radial paper's law concerns polygons conditioned on length, not walks of fixed length.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct, still open: (1) the count c_n = |W_n| and its asymptotics, including the connective constant's role in the count and any polynomial correction; the paper uses c_n only through c_n ρ^n ≥ 1 and submultiplicativity, and takes the connective constant from Duminil-Copin and Smirnov. (2) Explicit functions or constants: every statement carries C_{δ,k}, n_0(δ,k) and n^{±δ} or n^{o(1)} slack, so the exponents are not established as exact limits. (3) Endpoint displacement |γ_n - o| at fixed length: the Mass paper states it does not prove a fixed-length lower bound on this, and a diameter lower bound does not imply far-apart endpoints; the Renewal paper gives endpoint distance only on a density-one set of lengths. (4) Scaling limits: the Mass paper includes no convergence to a continuum curve and no continuum Hausdorff dimension; it does not identify an SLE limit. (5) Other lattices, dimensions, or universality across lattices, which the paper excludes. (6) Any interpretation of 'model' beyond exponent-level scaling of diameter, local mass and covering number.
entries.direction: proves the predicted 3/4 size exponent and the 4/3 mass and covering exponents for uniform fixed-length honeycomb walks (scaling exponents, up to n^{±δ}; not a count or formula)
entries.conditional_on: Yes. The Mass paper's proof uses three companion manuscripts in this family, cited but not proved in it: (a) 'Critical strip-crossing mass on the honeycomb lattice' (its Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 2.1 as quoted in the Mass paper): the boundary flux identity, B_h ≍ (1+h)^{-1/4} and m_h ≍ h^{3/4}; the normalization lemma's proof argues by contradiction from the bridge lower bound B_h ≍ h^{-1/4}. (b) 'Cylinder loop weights and planar nesting' (Lemma 11.4, Theorems 11.2 and 8.1, Corollaries 8.2 and 11.3, Proposition 11.5): the length-nest normalization, the raw first-length mass at most h^{13/12+o(1)}, and the all-count cylinder tail bound used for polygon families. (c) 'Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds' (Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 8.3): the polygon length-square mass bound H^{2/3+o(1)} and the uniform one-arc bound. External inputs: Duminil-Copin and Smirnov (2012) for the value of ρ, and Kesten's renewal method as presented by Madras and Slade for bridge factorization. The Renewal paper's finite bridge inputs come from its companion 'Uniform marked-polygon estimates and sharp finite bridge moments' (Theorem 1.1), and its every-length diameter upper bound (its uniform-law diameter clause) and several geometric lemmas come from the Mass paper's Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 4.1.
entries.doubts: The sections I read (introduction, inputs, completion) carry no sketch or hedge markers. I did not read the middle sections (sewing, probes, slow paths, roughly 3,000 lines), so I cannot report their internal status. Points the text itself bears on: (1) every claim is an n^{±δ} or n^{o(1)} statement with non-explicit constants C_{δ,k} and n_0(δ,k). (2) The proof's analytic content is delegated to the three companion manuscripts, so the strength of the Mass result equals that of those inputs as cited. (3) The Mass paper proves the diameter lower bound n^{3/4-δ} at every large n, while the Renewal paper states its endpoint-distance and maximum-radius laws for uniform full-plane walks only on a density-one set of lengths. The two papers do not cross-reference each other on this point (Renewal cites Mass for its diameter upper bound and several lemmas, and Mass does not cite Renewal), so the different length qualifications are not reconciled in the text. (4) The family contains overlapping claims: the H^{2/3+o(1)} length-square mass bound appears in both the Marked polygon and Signed manuscripts, and the 1/6 and 1/12 exponents appear in both the Cylinder loop weights and Signed manuscripts, so these are not independent confirmations of each other.
